Part 1 · Foundations

What is software architecture?

The significant decisions about how a system is organised: its main parts, how they connect, the qualities it must achieve, and the rules that keep it coherent.

“Significant” means costly to change later.

Architecture is trade-offs

DecisionGainsCosts
Cache data on the phoneFaster screensData may be stale
Queue payment confirmationsSurvives outagesSlight delay, more parts

Every decision gains one quality and costs another.

Part 1 · Foundations

What good documentation is

✗ A complete design spec written once up front

✗ A copy of the code in prose

✗ A document nobody updates

✓ Write down what is hard to see in the code: boundaries, qualities, decisions, reasons.

Part 1 · Foundations

Machines are readers too

  • Coding agents follow the context files you give them
  • Auto-generated files tended to lower success and raised cost by over 20% in one 2026 study
  • Developer-written files helped a little, but still cost more
  • Lesson: write only what the code can’t tell, and keep it short

Gloaguen et al., ETH Zurich, February 2026, arXiv:2602.11988 (preprint). Tested on Python repositories; results may differ elsewhere.

Part 1 · Foundations

Stakeholders and concerns

Stakeholder: a person, group or organisation with an interest in the system.

Concern: something a stakeholder cares about, such as “Can I recover a lost order?” or “Can I deploy on Friday?”

If nobody has a concern about it, don’t document it.

Part 1 · Foundations

Views and viewpoints

View: a representation of the system that answers a set of concerns.

Viewpoint: the convention for such views: what to show and in which notation.

A city has a road map, a metro map and a utilities map. Same city, different maps for different people.

arc42’s sections are in effect a ready-made set of views plus supporting text. ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 formalises these ideas.

Zoom levels (the C4 idea)

LevelShows
1 ContextThe system as one box, with people and systems around it
2 ContainersRunnable or deployable pieces
3 ComponentsInside one container
4 CodeRarely documented

Part 1 · Foundations

Two words that confuse beginners

Container: a runtime thing you start, such as an application or a data store. Not necessarily Docker.

Component: a grouping of related functionality behind a defined interface, inside a container.

arc42 is notation-neutral. Today: arc42 Level 1 ≈ containers and main blocks, Level 2 ≈ components.

Part 1 · Foundations

What is arc42?

  • A free, open-source template for architecture documentation
  • Created by Gernot Starke and Peter Hruschka
  • A structure, not a method: you still do the architecture
  • Not all 12 sections are mandatory. Size it to your system.

Part 1 · Foundations

Our running example: Doubles-to-Go

A web app where customers in Trinidad pre-order doubles and other street food from nearby vendors, pay online and collect without queuing.

  • Users: customers (phone, often 3G) and vendors (phone, busy hands)
  • Assumed scale: about 200 vendors, 20,000 customers, lunchtime peak
  • Neighbours: payment provider, SMS gateway

You’ll see it documented section by section. Then you do the same for your own system.

Warm-up (10 min)

  1. Draw You → Your phone → Messaging app as a Mermaid graph, with one labelled arrow
  2. Write a 3-row Markdown table of your team’s names and roles

Done when both render without errors.

Experienced? Add a sequence diagram of one real flow from your own system.

  3. Is a Docker image a “container” in C4 terms?
  4. Which arc42 section answers “what can’t we change?”
  5. Give one trade-off from your own work

notes: Ask for one hard-to-change choice from the room: database, language, one app or many.
Nuance: when the repositories’ other documentation was removed, generated files did help. They mostly compensate for missing docs. So good documentation comes first, and agent files stay minimal.

Goals and constraints shape the strategy. The strategy guides the building blocks, which are framed by the context. Behaviour, placement and shared rules follow from the blocks. Decisions explain the strategy, and quality scenarios test the goals. Section 11 risks track what could go wrong across all of it. Get section 1 wrong and everything downstream drifts.
